page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-512GB is an x86_64 architecture instance from the Cloud Native server family, running on KVM hypervisors. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, offering 64 shared vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with one thread per core. Memory capacity is substantial at 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. It includes no bundled local storage, no dedicated GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage setups for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and aggregate computational output. In PassMark, the server attains a strong overall CPU score of 65,693.58, extended instructions score of 88,380.14, and encryption score of 69,611.9. Multi-threaded decompression in bzip3 reaches 462.89 GB/sec (top 25%), while Clang compilation and ray tracing score strongly in Geekbench at 39,198.0 and 64,474.0 respectively. Redis SET performance is also elevated, recording 67.51 million operations per second. In contrast, single-core metrics reflect the lower 2.0 GHz base frequency, showing poor stress-ng single-core performance (772.19, bottom 10%) and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1,284.0.

Memory throughput reaches 145.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 86.79 GB/sec for writes, both falling within average ranges alongside a 2,076.7 PassMark memory score. For large language models, prompt processing scales moderately at 2,288.55 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but medium 7B model generation is limited to 6.22 tokens/sec (bottom 10%), highlighting the limitations of running multi-billion-parameter generation on shared CPU threads without accelerators.

Cost efficiency relies on dense RAM allocation and wide multi-core availability rather than raw per-thread latency. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration fits large-scale memory-intensive workloads, including distributed in-memory caching tiers, large database replicas, compilation clusters, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines that prioritize total memory footprint and throughput over low-latency single-thread execution.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-512GB is a memory-optimized cloud server based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running on KVM. It features 64 shared vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 512.0 GB of RAM, no local storage, and no GPU hardware. The server provides 8.0 GB of RAM per core, emphasizing high aggregate memory capacity. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high parallel throughput, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 65,693.58, 462.89 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 67.51 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, single-core metrics fall lower, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring in the bottom 10% (772.19). Given its substantial memory ratio and multi-threaded throughput, the instance is suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching, code compilation farms, and batch processing tasks.
